newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RTZ-CRA says Century talks fail.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RTZ-CRA says Century talks fail.

text.p: Mining house RTZ-CRA said on Friday that talks with aboriginal groups over development of the massive Century zinc mine in the state of Queensland collapsed overnight.
"We obviously are disappointed that the negotiations did not produce a result," a spokesman for RTZ-CRA subsidiary Century Zinc Ltd told Reuters.
Negotiations will now shift to the Federal native title tribunal where a binding agreement can take up to six months.

CRA and the Queensland government have withdrawn a A$60 million jobs and compensation package which was offered during the talks, said Rick Farley, the lead negotiator for the 12 aboriginal groups involved in the talks.
The company had set a deadline of Thursday midnight (1300 GMT) for agreement with the groups to proceed with development of the A$1 billion mine.
"The situation now is that only four out of the 12 claimants had signed the agreement by the midnight deadline," Farley said.
"Subsequently the company and the Queensland government have withdrawn their offer," he said.
It was still possible to reach an agreement in the next few days that could be presented to Century Zinc for approval, thus avoiding arbitration in the tribunal.
"That is possible but just how likely is another question," Farley said.
